newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil exporter groups choose commission members.
newsitem.headline: Brazil exporter groups choose commission members.

text.p: Brazil's two coffee exporter bodies have chosen their representatives for a six-member commission which will discuss the possible creation of a new, united institution, exporter officials said.
Representing Brazilian Coffee Exporters Federation (Febec) will be Oswaldo Aranha, Bruno Angst and Salvador Costa, said Aranha, Febec's president.
Representing Brazilian Coffee Exporters Association (Abecafe) will be Abecafe president Jorge Esteve and directors Joaquim Libanio and Urs Wegmann, Abecafe said in a statement.
"The commission will evaluate if the formation of a new entity will strengthen the sector, enabling it to search for solutions to key problems," the Abecafe statement said.
Febec has traditionally been the representative exporters' body and as such has a seat on Brazil's new coffee council, the CDPC.
But in November 1995 a group of exporters formed Abecafe, principally because they opposed a private sector plan dividing out coffee exports internally.
The association has gradually grown in size and now has 45 members, accounting for around 47 percent of Brazilian coffee exports in 1996, according to Abecafe statistics.
Last week members of Febec decided to hold talks with Abecafe to see if it would be possible to set up a new entity which would meet the needs of both groups.
No date has been set for the first meeting of the commission, Aranha said.
